notes.summary: Intrinsic compact primary sections, exact gauge cocycle, finite lifting and conductor fibres on all semivaluations; Noetherian completion preserves sections and primary ideals.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs the boundary without assuming minimal support, resolution, or characteristic zero. The conductor-infinite stratum is closed; its finite complement is only open. Completion invariance holds for every Noetherian local ring. Dimension-zero reduction has empty centred boundary.
notes.text:
Let (R,m) be Noetherian local and a proper m-primary ideal. Semivaluations have values in [0,infinity], are multiplicative, satisfy the ultrametric inequality, send 0 to infinity and 1 to zero, and satisfy 0<v(m)<infinity. Their supports are primes strictly below m, not necessarily minimal. Values of finitely generated ideals are minima over generators; expressing generators through another generating set proves independence. Consequently v(IJ)=v(I)+v(J) and v(I+J)=min(v(I),v(J)). Units have value zero.

The semivaluation axioms define closed conditions in the compact Hausdorff product [0,infinity]^R: extended addition and minimum are continuous and the order relation is closed. The equation v(m)=1 is closed. If m^r is contained in a and a is contained in m^s, then s v(m)<=v(a)<=r v(m). Rescaling therefore identifies the compact m-section with V_a(R). Every primary ideal gauge is positive, finite, continuous and bounded there. For another primary b, H_ab(v)=v/v(b) is a homeomorphism with bounded positive denominator and bounded reciprocal. Direct substitution proves its inverse and H_bd H_ab=H_ad. A degree-one homogeneous function transforms by h_b(H_ab(v))=h_a(v)/v(b). Nonprimary gauges give only the open domain where their value is positive and finite; unit and zero ideals have no level-one section.

Nilpotents have infinite value, and applying the ultrametric inequality in both directions proves v(f+n)=v(f) for nilpotent n. Reduction preserves the entire boundary and every ideal gauge. A zero-dimensional local reduction is a field and has empty centred boundary. For positive-dimensional excellent reduced R, a penultimate prime in a saturated chain gives a one-dimensional excellent domain quotient. Its finite normalization has a local DVR factor, giving a point of every primary section. The ordinary excellence consequences used are quotient and finite-type localization stability, universal catenarity and the Nagata finiteness property; none implies resolution in arbitrary characteristic.

For a finite reduced injection R into B, every boundary semivaluation lifts. Choose P in B over its support p and the finite field extension L=Frac(B/P) over K=Frac(R/p). Let A be the valuation ring in K, choose a prime over its maximal ideal in its integral closure A' in L, and a valuation ring W dominating that localization. The domination argument is elementary Zorn: a maximal dominating local subring is a valuation ring because, for every x, its maximal ideal remains proper in the extension by x or by x inverse. Indeed, a relation 1=sum a_i x^(-i), with coefficients in the maximal ideal, makes x integral; lying over then makes the ideal proper in the extension by x. Localization contradicts maximality unless x or its inverse already belongs. This is also the complete inspected immediate argument in Swanson–Huneke 6.4.1–6.4.2, printed126–127. W intersects K in A: an element outside A has inverse in the maximal ideal of A and hence of W. An algebraic equation shows two least terms have equal value, so a positive integer multiple of each new value belongs to the old real value group. Division and common multiples define the order-preserving real extension. Integral elements have nonnegative value by the unique-smallest-leading-term argument. Giving P infinite value supplies the required semivaluation on B. Restriction is therefore a continuous compact surjection and a quotient map, retaining all supports.

For finite normalization S of reduced excellent R, the conductor c=(R:S) contains a regular element by denominator clearing, is an ideal of both rings, and R=S times_(S/c) (R/c). An element of S whose residue comes from R differs from an element of R by an element of c, proving the identity. The boundary of S is the finite disjoint union of local normal-centre sections above m. Idempotents select minimal components, and localization at a centre changes no denominator values. Chinese-remainder lifts separating centres and their complements show that centre pieces are clopen. Local normalization centres, rather than irreducible components alone, index the branches.

If v(c)<infinity, choose c0 in c of finite value. Every lift is determined by w(s)=v(c0 s)-v(c0), with a finite second term, so the fibre is a singleton. If v(c)=infinity, all lifts kill c; equality of restrictions through S/c to R/c is precisely the remaining equivalence relation. The infinity stratum is CLOSED and its finite complement OPEN, without a claim that the complement is closed. Continuous fibre-constant functions descend continuously through the compact quotient. Extended nonpositive upper semicontinuous fibre-constant functions also descend upper semicontinuously, since their closed superlevel sets have compact images. This is topology, not a positivity theorem.

Completion needs no excellence. For F in Rhat choose F_N modulo m^N and put d=v(m)>0. The estimate v(F_M-F_N)>=Nd implies either finite stabilization when v(F_N)<Nd, or convergence to infinity. The limit defines vhat(F), independently of representatives, and min(vhat(F),Nd)=min(v(F_N),Nd). Representatives of sums and products prove all semivaluation axioms, including infinity; a completed unit has a unit representative modulo m. The truncation identities force uniqueness. Composing with q(t)=t/(1+t), q(infinity)=1, gives continuous truncations with uniform error at most 1/(1+N/r), since d>=1/r. Thus completion restriction is a homeomorphism on ALL semivaluations. Every completed primary J contains m^N Rhat; lifting its generators through R/m^N=Rhat/m^N Rhat proves J=(J intersect R)Rhat. The same quotient argument proves contraction of a primary extension recovers the original ideal. Corresponding ideal functions, uniform cones and decreasing completions agree exactly; no model-category equivalence is asserted.

The full artifact is n1.md, incorporated in argument.md and P12.2-paper.tex. Rerun python audit_inputs.py and python build_delivery.py. These are unverified mathematical drafts using the explicitly disclosed ordinary algebraic background; successful commands do not prove correctness.

notes.summary: Exact-domain algebraic source applications: ideal integrality, common exponents, Rees residual degree, dimension formula, normal completion and general Izumi–Rees bounds.
notes.detailedSummary: All minimal components and zero-dimensional quotient components are qualified explicitly. The order bound is derived for nonzero nonunits, with units handled separately. Published applications use inspected immediate units; original Rees1989 and historical dependency proofs were not independently read.
notes.text:
Use n1's section and reduction conventions. The bound Swanson–Huneke author PDF is the CURRENT file created July2024, not a claim of byte identity with the 2006 printing.

The complete immediate 6.8.1–6.8.4 units, printed139–140, give the following application. Let E be Noetherian semilocal, J contain a boundary power, and Q be finitely generated. Suppose w(Q)>=w(J) at every normalized centred semivaluation, and Q has zero image on every zero-dimensional minimal component on which J is nonunit. Then Q is contained in the integral closure of J. Apply the centred rank-one DVR criterion to each positive-dimensional minimal component and each local centre. On zero-dimensional components the boundary vanishes; in all subsequent applications Q=K(aE)^L with L>0, so its image is zero. Unit J-components are automatic. The zero-dimensional condition cannot be omitted simply because that component has empty boundary. For nonreduced E, lift componentwise integral equations, multiply over all finitely many minimal primes, and raise the nilpotent error to a power. This produces an actual monic equation with degree-i coefficients in J^i. The finite-minimal-prime argument of1.1.5 was inspected, and PDF pixels on printed140 confirmed the integral-closure bars.

If Q is integral over J, each qt satisfies a homogeneous monic equation over E[Jt]. Thus E[(J+Q)t] is a finite graded module over E[Jt]. Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most h. In degree N+h, each coefficient belongs to J^(N+h-d), contained in J^N. Therefore Q^(N+h) is contained in J^N for every N>=1. This proof works on nonreduced rings and asserts no finiteness of the whole normalized Rees algebra. The complete immediate reduction chain1.2.3–1.2.5 was also inspected; printed6 confirms the missing overbar in the extracted criterion.

For nonzero primary ideals in an excellent local DOMAIN, use Theorem10.2.2 through the complete ending Proposition10.2.3, printed200–202, for Rees DVR existence. Proposition10.4.3 and its complete proof, printed209–210, give residue transcendence degree dim(A)-1 at formally equidimensional domain hypotheses. Excellence supplies universal catenarity, and the complete immediate B.5.1 unit, printed418–419, supplies its equivalence with local formal equidimensionality and the finite-type dimension formula. In particular, for a finite-type birational DOMAIN B over excellent local domain A and P over m, dim(B_P)+trdeg_(A/m) kappa(P)=dim(A). B.3.2's statement and context were read; its proof refers to a modification of an earlier argument, which is not described as independently read.

The entire official Stacks0C23 lemma/proof says that a normal Noetherian local ring with normal formal fibres has normal completion; excellent suffices. Its immediate proof refers to Algebra10.163.8, not supplied or independently read here. A normal completed local ring is a domain, so excellent NORMAL local A is analytically irreducible and analytically unramified. No such assertion is made for arbitrary nonnormal domains.

The complete pages1–2 context of exact Rond–Spivakovsky arXiv1404.4885v1 was inspected: Definitions1.1–1.2, Theorems1.3,1.4,1.7 and Remark1.6. Theorem1.3 compares divisorial valuations on any analytically irreducible local DOMAIN, not merely a complete domain. Let nu be centred divisorial and nu_j the finitely many m-Rees valuations. Choose c_j with nu(f)<=c_j nu_j(f), and C0=max_j c_j nu_j(m). Then nu(f)<=C0 min_j nu_j(f)/nu_j(m)=C0 asymptotic_ord_m(f)<=C0(ord_m(f)+K), by1.4 and1.7. For nonzero nonunits ord_m(f)>=1, giving nu(f)<=C0(1+K)ord_m(f). Units have both values zero and are handled separately. The literal STRICT Remark1.6 would fail on units and is not used. Swanson Rees Valuations' complete Section5, printed17–18, was read: its5.2 states only a complete-domain version. The general application uses exact Rond–Spivakovsky1.3, not an extension of5.2. Original Rees1989 and historical Izumi proofs have NOT been independently read.

These are precise ordinary published applications, with disclosed historical dependencies, not source grants inferred from metadata. They establish no singular SNC retractions or positive-characteristic resolution. Artifact n2.md and source-application-ledger.md retain complete domains and qualifications. Exact excerpts and viewed images are under source-excerpts and reports. Rerun python audit_inputs.py; extraction and hash matching are not mathematical verification.

notes.summary: Separates raw P,Q, continuous C and decreasing D; reconstructs the corrected density lattice and all-support normal-target norm trace.
notes.detailedSummary: The rational difference span is a lattice, while its uniform closure is a real vector lattice. Norm coefficients use generic inseparable lengths and finite integral closures, retaining nonzero supports. Normal targets have exact fibre-constant C and D descent, including vertical source components.
notes.text:
Define P(A) as finite nonnegative REAL sums of positive gauges v(I), for ideals containing a boundary power, with units allowed. Put Q=-P, C=the uniform closure of Q, and D=infima of nonempty decreasing C-nets, including zero and bottom. On a finite semilocal algebra these are finite products over local closed centres: tuples of ideals glue in an Artinian quotient by a common boundary power. Rational profiles -v(I)/k are dense in C, since rational approximation and common denominators turn finite sums into product-ideal profiles. C is a closed convex cone of finite continuous nonpositive functions, stable under finite maxima by ideal sums. D is upper semicontinuous and closed under positive scaling, addition and finite maxima through product directed sets. No increasing-limit or arbitrary-infimum closure is assumed.

The rational difference span is a lattice. After a common denominator every element is (v(I)-v(J))/d, and min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH). All ideals still contain boundary powers. It contains rational constants and separates points through v((f)+a^N)=min(v(f),N). Its UNIFORM CLOSURE is a real vector lattice; arbitrary finite real spans are not silently given integer ideal expressions. The compact lattice approximation argument gives density in all continuous functions: affine combinations of a separating gauge match a target at two points, rational approximation preserves local error bounds, and finite minima and maxima over neighbourhood covers give a uniform approximation.

Let A be excellent normal local DOMAIN, A subset B a finite DOMAIN extension, K subset L the fraction fields and n=[L:K]. For a B-ideal J choose finite A-module generators b_l. Let N(J) be the coefficient ideal of Norm_(L(T)/K(T))(sum T_l b_l). For the K-embeddings Sigma of L in an algebraic closure and q=n/|Sigma|, the polynomial factors as product_sigma(sum T_l sigma(b_l))^q. Over an algebraic closure, the tensor algebra is a product of Artinian factors of length q, and multiplication has determinant the residue scalar to that length. Coefficients are integral over A and lie in K, hence belong to A. Linear substitutions in both directions prove generator independence.

Take a finite field M containing all embedding images and its finite integral closure E over A. Extend a base semivaluation to E using n1, retaining its support. Never attempt to extend a nonzero-support semivaluation to the original fraction field. Polynomial coefficient-minimum values multiply: quotient by support, pass to the valued fraction field, divide by a least-valued coefficient, and reduce; nonzero residue polynomials have nonzero product. A factor vanishing modulo support gives infinite coefficient value and the same identity. Thus v(N(J))=q sum_sigma w_sigma(J). If J contains a boundary power, adding x in a^N as redundant generator puts x^n in N(J); hence N(J) contains a boundary power and has finite continuous gauge.

The positive measure mu_v=q sum_sigma delta_(w_sigma) has mass n. Its integrals on all ideal gauges are determined by the norm identity; density and common mass prove independence on every continuous test. Its support is exactly the restriction fibre. For the reverse inclusion, extend any given B-fibre valuation to E with the identity embedding; E is integral and finite over B, so the identity summand assigns that point positive mass. Choice independence proves every fibre point has positive mass, and there are at most n points. Multiplicities are generic inseparable lengths, not defectless e f formulas at arbitrary real valuations.

T(H)(v)=integral H dmu_v is positive, has norm n, and sends continuous functions to continuous functions: first use gauges, then uniform density and the mass bound. It maps -w(J)/k to -v(N(J))/k, preserving C. A finite positive sum commutes with decreasing nonpositive extended limits, preserving descent of fibre-constant D-functions without cancellation of opposite infinities.

For a reduced finite injection into normal local A, retain minimal source components dominating A and normalize them. At least one exists by lying over zero. Sum their traces and divide by the sum of their generic degrees. For a fibre-constant C or D target, every traced value is exactly its descended value on EVERY base semivaluation. Vertical components receive no invented generic degree; constancy on the FULL original fibre makes them harmless for this descent argument. Thus normal targets have exact C,D image equal to the fibre-constant subclass. Every extension has the same primary-gauge denominator, giving the exact gauge cocycle.

The complete supplied norm/trace proof units were read as DATA and independently reconstructed; their incorrect arbitrary-real-span lattice wording is repaired above. Artifact n3.md contains the full argument; rerun python build_delivery.py. This does not construct a geometric trace on arbitrary nonnormal targets.

notes.summary: Bounded uniform C descends exactly along every excellent reduced finite injection iff fibre constant, including nonisolated and infinite conductors.
notes.detailedSummary: Dimension induction uses approximate quotient-ideal integral dependence, common exponents and the exact conductor fibre-product residue identity. Dyadic profiles are internal approximation devices. Raw downstairs and normalization cones share their uniform closure but need not coincide.
notes.text:
For every excellent reduced local R and reduced nonzero finite injection into B, f* C(R) equals the fibre-constant subclass of C(B), and pullback is an isometry. Induct on target dimension. Dimension zero has empty boundary; normal targets are n3. First prove normalization descent in dimension d from arbitrary finite-injection descent below d, then recover arbitrary injections by normal-base change.

Let S normalize R, c its conductor, C0=R/c and E=S/c. A regular conductor element gives dim(C0)<d. C0 into E remains injective after reduction, since nilpotence is detected in an injected subring. For fibre-constant u in C(S), let h be its continuous descent. Restriction to E lies in C(E), and dimension induction descends it to h0 in C(C0). If that section is empty, every base point has finite conductor value and no quotient estimate is needed.

Fix eps>0. Approximate u and h0 within eps by rational profiles j=-w(J)/k and kappa=-v(K)/k, synchronizing denominators by powers and making 1/k<eps. Multiplication of J by aS at arbitrarily large denominator ensures proper contraction with arbitrarily small extra error; start with tighter errors to absorb it. Zero has its direct zero model. On E, |w(K_E)-w(J_E)|<2k eps. Choose integer L with 2k eps<L<=2k eps+1, so L/k<3eps. For Q=K_E(aE)^L, every normalized semivaluation satisfies w(Q)>=w(J_E). The positive boundary factor kills Q on zero-dimensional minimal components; n2 therefore gives Q contained in integral_closure(J_E). A common h' satisfies Q^(N+h') contained in J_E^N for every N.

Set I_N=J^N intersect R. It contains a^(MN) for some M and is proper, hence primary. The conductor fibre product gives the EXACT residue identity (I_N+c)/c=J_E^N intersect C0: a residue on the right lifts to an element of J^N whose residue comes from C0, and that lift belongs to R. Consequently K^(N+h')(aC0)^(L(N+h')) is contained in this image.

At v(c)=infinity the quotient semivaluation gives v(I_N)/(kN)<=(1+h'/N)(v(K)/k+L/k). At finite conductor value the unique lift w and cJ^N contained in I_N give w(J)/k<=v(I_N)/(kN)<=w(J)/k+v(c)/(kN). ONLY this finite-conductor estimate divides conductor value by N. On every point, I_N contained in J^N gives v(I_N)/(kN)>=-h(v)-eps. Thus the dyadic b_n=v(I_(2^n))/(k2^n) decrease, have pointwise infimum between -h-eps and -h+4eps, and are finite continuous. Their monotonicity follows from I_N^2 contained in I_(2N). The increasing open sets {b_n+h<5eps} cover the compact section, so one index covers it entirely. Together with the lower bound this gives uniform error at most5eps for -b_n versus h. Let eps tend to zero. The negative dyadic profiles INCREASE internally; they are not decreasing regularization.

For arbitrary R into B, form B'=(B tensor_R S)_red. Its spectrum surjects onto Spec S, so its kernel in reduced S is zero. The pulled-back u is fibre constant over S, since equal S-restrictions imply equal underlying R-restrictions. Apply n3 on every normal local centre to descend into C(S); the result is exactly h pulled back to S. Normalization descent then gives h in C(R). This closes induction. Pullback inclusion is ideal extension; surjectivity gives the isometry.

If Q_R is the raw negative downstairs cone and N_R the continuous descended functions whose normalization restrictions lie in the RAW local cones, then Q_R subset N_R subset C_R and both raw cones have uniform closure C_R. No raw equality is asserted. All conductor-quotient fibres and nonminimal supports are retained. The argument reconstructs ROOT317 rather than importing its label as support. Artifact n4.md contains the full proof; rerun python build_delivery.py. The arbitrary incompatible-ideal contraction shortcut is false, as n10 independently demonstrates.

notes.summary: Everywhere strictly negative fibre-constant unbounded D-functions descend, including minus-infinity; continuous insertion produces an actual decreasing C-net.
notes.detailedSummary: The proof uses upper semicontinuity and compact strict tests, rather than uniform convergence to an unbounded limit. Increasing dyadic approximants remain internal. Real positive scaling yields strict majorants; their downward-directed set represents the target.
notes.text:
For an excellent reduced finite injection R into B, fibre-constant u in D(B) descends into D(R) when its descent h is everywhere strictly negative. Values minus-infinity and discontinuity are allowed. By n1 h is upper semicontinuous; compactness gives h<=-c0 for some c0>0. All-bottom is directly the limit of negative integer multiples of the boundary gauge, and zero descends separately. Normal targets follow from n3's finite positive trace. Induct on dimension as in n4, first normalization from lower-dimensional finite-injection descent, then reduced normalization base change.

For normalization S with conductor c, C0=R/c and E=S/c, restrict a decreasing C(S)-net to E and descend its limit by induction to h0 in D(C0). We prove insertion: for every finite continuous F>h on the base section there is q in C(R) with h<q<F. The extended lower semicontinuous gap F-h has a positive finite lower bound e. Choose one continuous C(S)-majorant g from the decreasing net with u<=g<-c0/2 and g<F pulled back-e/2. Strict-test open sets cover the compact section, and directedness supplies one common index; this is not uniform convergence to u.

Choose b in (0,1/2) with b||g||<e/8. The scaled (1-b)g stays below F-e/4 and exceeds finite u by b c0/2. Uniform rational-profile approximation with sufficiently small error yields j=-w(J)/k, uniformly negative, and s>0 with u+s<=j<F pulled back-e/8. At bottom points the lower inequality is automatic. J is proper at every positive-dimensional centre and contains a boundary power. Put M=||j||.

For arbitrarily small delta>0 obtain a rational quotient profile kappa=-v(K)/k with h0<=kappa and its E-pullback<j restricted to E+delta. To prove existence, take a decreasing continuous net g_i to h0 and b1 in (0,1/2) with b1 M<s/4. Since u_E<=j_E-s, (1-b1)u_E<j_E-s/4. Compactness on E selects i with (1-b1)g_i pulled back<j_E-s/8, while compactness on C0 selects simultaneously g_i<-c0/2. Scaling makes it exceed h0 by b1 c0/2; uniform approximation with error below min(b1 c0/4,s/16) gives kappa. Synchronize J,K denominators and enlarge k so1/k<delta. Empty quotient section needs no construction.

Choose integer L with k delta<L<=k delta+1. Q=K_E(aE)^L satisfies all valuation inequalities against J_E; its positive boundary factor handles zero-dimensional components. N2 gives integral dependence and Q^(N+h') contained in J_E^N. Contract I_N=J^N intersect R and use n4's proved exact residue identity. At infinite conductor value, liminf[-v(I_N)/(kN)]>=kappa(v)-2delta>=h(v)-2delta. At finite conductor value the conductor estimate gives limit j(w)>=h+s. No infinity is divided by N.

The dyadic profiles f_n=-v(I_(2^n))/(k2^n) are finite continuous, INCREASE, satisfy f_n<=j on every lift, and have limit>=h-2delta. The increasing sets {f_n>h-3delta} are OPEN because h is upper semicontinuous and cover the compact section, including bottom points. Select one n valid everywhere. Take delta small enough that eta=3delta/c0<1/2 and eta M<e/16. Then q=(1-eta)f_n belongs to C(R). At finite h<=-c0, q>(1-eta)(h-3delta)>=h+eta c0-3delta(1-eta)=h+3delta eta>h. At bottom q is finite. Since f_n<=j and j>=-M, q<j+e/16<F. The coefficient is a real positive scale, justified by uniform rational approximation; it need not be rational.

Let Q consist of continuous C(R)-functions strictly above h. Zero belongs. For q1,q2 use the continuous TEST min(q1,q2) in insertion to get another member below both; the minimum itself is not asserted psh. Thus Q is downward directed. At each v and finite t>h(v), upper semicontinuity and compact Hausdorff normality give continuous F>h with F(v)<t: choose a level between h(v) and t, a neighbourhood where h lies below it, and a Urysohn cutoff interpolating to a global strict upper bound outside. Insertion gives q(v)<t. Hence inf Q=h, and reverse pointwise order gives an ACTUAL decreasing C-net. This completes normalization and finite-injection induction without flattening completed nets or using an increasing-limit closure.

Artifact n5.md contains the complete reconstruction of ROOT319, with n4 used for its proved residue identity and base-change algebra. Rerun python build_delivery.py. Mixed-zero descent is a separate theorem in n6.

notes.summary: Full D fibre-image equality for every excellent reduced finite injection, including mixed zeros, partial/all bottom and every support.
notes.detailedSummary: Direct divisorial density and exact-domain Izumi–Rees give the normal-branch zero dichotomy. The active indicator descends through the proved bounded theorem. Strict descent plus scaling and maxima supplies exact-zero-off-active majorants and a genuine decreasing net. Geometric transfer still depends on n8.
notes.text:
The theorem is f*D_a(R)={u in D_(aB)(B): u is constant on every restriction fibre} for every excellent reduced local R and reduced nonzero finite injection into B. It concerns the ideal-uniform decreasing class, not an independently certified geometric class.

First prove divisorial density on an excellent local DOMAIN A. Fix v in its primary section and finitely many strict coordinate tests. Choose a generator a0 of a with v(a0)=1. Include a_j/a0 and, for rational lower and finite upper tests p/q<v(f)<r/s, include f^q/a0^p and a0^r/f^s in a finite-type birational subalgebra B0 of Frac(A). At an infinity coordinate retain only a rational lower test. Units and the zero element have fixed values. All denominators have finite value, so v extends nonnegatively to B0 even at nonzero support. Its positive-value prime P contains a0 and every strict-test ratio. Thus (B0)_P is excellent local domain of positive dimension. Take a Rees DVR of its maximal ideal using n2. Its valuation nu is positive on P and nonnegative on B0. Hence nu(a)=nu(a0)>0, and rescaling by this value satisfies every original strict test.

It is divisorial OVER A, not merely over the chart. N2's birational dimension formula gives dim((B0)_P)+trdeg_(A/m) kappa(P)=dim(A). The Rees DVR has residue transcendence degree dim((B0)_P)-1 over kappa(P). Additivity gives dim(A)-1 over A/m. Its group is discrete rank one and its centre on A is m because the primary ideal has positive value. This proves density in the actual pointwise topology, including nonminimal supports, without singular SNC or arbitrary-characteristic resolution.

For excellent NORMAL local A, n2 gives analytic irreducibility and, for each centred divisorial nu, nu(f)<=C_nu ord_m(f) for nonzero nonunits, with units zero separately. Normalize nu by a and absorb that denominator into C_nu. If m^r is contained in a, then v0(m)>=1/r and v0(f)>=ord_m(f)v0(m) at every v0, including nonminimal support. For proper primary I choose nonzero f attaining its finite v0-value. Therefore nu(I)<=C_nu r v0(I). The unit ideal also satisfies this. Passing from raw profiles through finite real sums and uniform closure gives g(nu)>=C_nu r g(v0) for every g in C(A). If g(v0)=0, nonpositivity gives zero at every divisorial nu; density and continuity imply g=0. For u=inf g_i in D, u(v0)=0 forces each nonpositive g_i(v0)=0 and therefore each g_i=0. Thus every normal local D-function is either zero everywhere or strictly negative everywhere, bottom included. Upper semicontinuity and compactness give a negative upper bound for each nonzero branch function.

Let u in D(S) be normalization-fibre constant. Its finitely many local normal-centre functions are zero or everywhere negative. Call the latter active, including bottom centres. Active and inactive points cannot share a fibre because their u-values have different signs. The tuple sigma=-1 on active centres and0 on inactive centres lies in C(S), realized by boundary gauges and componentwise units glued in an Artinian boundary quotient. It is fibre constant. Apply the independently proved n4 to descend sigma into C(R). This is the essential POSITIVITY descent, not a topological inference. T={sigma=-1} is clopen; the descended h is zero off T and <=-c on T for some c>0. Empty T gives zero directly.

For every delta>0, u-delta belongs to D(S) by product-directed addition, remains fibre constant and is everywhere strictly negative. N5 gives h-delta in D(R). This alone does not permit an increasing delta-limit. Instead take any finite continuous F>h on compact T, with positive finite lower gap e. Choose eta in (0,1/2) satisfying eta(||F||+e)<e/4, and delta=eta c/[2(1-eta)]. At finite h on T, (1-eta)(h-delta)=h+eta(-h-c/2)>h. Since h<=F-e, the bound on eta also gives (1-eta)(h-delta)<F-e/2. At bottom the upper inequality holds and every finite majorant exceeds h.

Choose a decreasing C(R)-net g_i to h-delta. The strict open tests (1-eta)g_i<F-e/4 cover T; compactness and directedness choose one i globally. Choose N>0 with -N<min_T F. Then q=max((1-eta)g_i,N sigma) belongs to C(R), satisfies h<q<F on T, and is EXACTLY zero=h off T. On T both terms are below F, while the first dominates the strictly larger scaled target at finite h; q is finite at bottom. Off T its second term is zero and its first nonpositive. Only positive scaling and maxima are used.

Let Q be these continuous C(R)-majorants, exactly zero off T and strictly above h on T. Zero belongs. The continuous TEST min(q1,q2) on T and the insertion just proved give a member below both, without assuming the minimum psh. The Urysohn test construction of n5 supplies arbitrarily low values above h at any chosen point of T. Thus inf Q=h on T and zero off T. Reverse pointwise order gives an ACTUAL decreasing C-net, proving full normalization descent, including mixed-zero and partial-bottom cases.
